### Observed differences

- The block A20, A21, A22, A24 and A25 ran in every trace in both windows, but moved from late to early: its mean position was about 0.63 of the trace in the earlier window and about 0.39 in the later window. [POS003, POS004, POS005, POS007, POS008]
- The group A19, A23, A26, A27 and A28 kept low, stable participation (each in roughly 16–25 in 100 traces, together about one per case) but moved from early to late: mean position about 0.31–0.36 earlier versus about 0.66–0.71 later. [POS002, POS006, POS009, POS010, POS011]
- The order between these activities and A29/A33 reversed almost completely: earlier, A29 preceded A20 in about 99 in 100 traces and A33 preceded A20 in about 995 in 1,000; later, A20 preceded A29 in about 98 in 100 and A33 in about 995 in 1,000. The same near-complete reversals hold for A21, A22, A24 and A25 against A29 and A33. [REL016, REL017, REL022, REL023, REL028, REL029, REL037, REL038, REL042, REL043]
- The two groups also reversed against each other: in traces containing both, A23, A26, A27 and A28 typically preceded A20/A21/A22/A24/A25 earlier (e.g. A23 before A20 in about 93 in 100 such traces) and typically followed them later. [REL012, REL013, REL018, REL019, REL024, REL025, REL030, REL034, REL039, REL044]
- The segment boundaries swapped. Earlier, the observed outgoing transitions of A19, A23, A26, A27 and A28 went almost entirely to A29 (about 93–100 in 100); later they go almost entirely to A34 (about 90–100 in 100). Earlier, A20/A21/A22/A24/A25 exited mainly to A34 (about 13–26 in 100 of their outgoing transitions); later they exit to A29 (about 18–24 in 100). [DIR003, DIR007, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR008, DIR009]
- The feeding activities swapped targets too: A33's outgoing transitions moved from essentially all pointing into the A20/A21/A22/A24/A25 block to essentially all pointing into the A19/A23/A26/A27/A28 group, while A44's moved from A06 plus the A19-group to the A20-block. A29 and A33 themselves kept roughly their places (mean positions about 0.36→0.48 and 0.54→0.67). [DIR013, DIR014, POS012, POS013]
- Short-range adjacency changed accordingly: A44 reached A29 within five steps in 200 of 200 earlier traces but 1 of 200 later; A24 reached A34 within five steps in 200 earlier versus 1 later; A25 reached A29 within five steps in 1 earlier versus 197 later; A44 reached A22 within five steps in 1 earlier versus 192 later. [LAG015, LAG004, LAG005, LAG013]
- Separately, A06 became rarer and rerouted: present in 30 in 100 traces earlier versus 12 in 100 later, with outgoing transitions shifting from mainly A23, A28, A27, A19 and A26 to mainly A48, A16 and A50, a more variable position, and the direct A44→A06 hand-off all but disappearing (about 53 traces earlier, 2 later). [OCC001, DIR001, POS001, LAG012]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that two segments of the process exchanged their order. In the earlier window, a case typically ran A44, then one of A19/A23/A26/A27/A28, then A29, then A33, then the block A20/A21/A22/A24/A25, closing towards A34; in the later window, the block A20/A21/A22/A24/A25 runs directly after A44, then A29 and A33, then one of A19/A23/A26/A27/A28, again closing towards A34. [REL016, REL017, DIR003, DIR004, DIR013, DIR014, POS003, POS012]

The rearrangement is shown directly and consistently: every cross-pair order reversal points the same way (REL), the boundary successors flip in step (DIR), and the position shifts move in opposite directions by roughly a quarter of the trace (POS). Participation is essentially unchanged — the A20-block occurs in all traces in both windows and the A19-group in about a fifth — so this is a reordering, not a shift in how often existing paths are taken. The screening volume also exceeds what a stable process produces: 93 items qualified where about 1 would be expected without change. [REL016, DIR007, POS004, LAG015, screening]

Limitations: the many agreeing items largely restate one underlying rearrangement rather than confirming it independently; the internal ordering of each block and the exact link between A29 and A33 are not directly resolved; POS and LAG use event positions, not clock time; and several LAG items rest on a single observed pair. A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that this exchange was one piece of a broader reconfiguration, since A06 changed separately in the same period. [LAG001, LAG009, LAG012, OCC001]

Other differences: A06 declined and rerouted — from 30 in 100 traces to 12 in 100, with outgoing transitions now mainly to A48, A16 and A50 instead of the A19/A23/A26/A27/A28 group — a distinct difference not covered by the exchange hypothesis. Routing at A14 → A15 and A49 → A50 stayed essentially unchanged, with only trace-level new edges appearing. [OCC001, DIR001, POS001, DIR002, DIR015]
